narr: Deep-layer ridging over the Southeast United States held up a trough over the Central United States for the first few days of April, leading to a prolonged and significant severe weather and flooding event from Texas to Ohio and West Virginia along a stalled boundary. As the ridge began to retreat eastward, a cold front slowly progressed through Central Alabama on April 6, with an all-hazards weather event unfolding. Slow moving thunderstorms from early morning to late afternoon resulted in flooding issues across northwestern counties and the Birmingham, Montgomery, and Auburn/Opelika areas. Additionally, two brief tornadoes were confirmed, and there were a few isolated reports of hail and wind damage. Late that evening, a motorist in Hale County drove into a downed tree, resulting in a fatality.
ev: Part of Victor Rd was washed out by a swollen creek.
A large portion of Dodson Circle was washed out.
A section of Mt. Pleasant Church Rd was washed out, and water was flowing over Highway 17 near Steedley Rd.
A large section of Ellenburg Rd in Haleyville was washed out.
Significant rise of Cottondale Creek in Cottonwood following heavy rain.
Heavy rainfall resulted in flooding issues in the Hoover area. The intersection of US Highway 31 and Alabama Highway 150 was flooded, with at least one stalled vehicle.

Valleydale Road near Veterans Park was impassable, with flooding along Acton Creek also impacting other nearby roadways. Just to the south, Cahaba Valley Creek east of Interstate 65 reached minor flood stage.
Flooding was reported at various locations across the city of Montgomery.
The 6500 block of Butler Mill Road collapsed due to floodwaters.
Various roadways around Auburn and Opelika became impassable due to floodwaters.
Water surrounded residences on 5th St South in Phenix City.
